To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The frequency of a signal recorded from a laser Dopplier anemometer depends on the size of the particles.
The frequency shift in laser Doppler systems depends on the size of the scattering particles and on the nature of their scattering function.

the size of the particles in the investigated region influences the frequency of a Doppler signal and that the influence of this factor is determined by the ratio of the particle size to the period of the interference fringes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical study of laser Doppler spectroscopic systems.
a theoretical analysis of the influence of the size of particles on the frequency of a laser Doppler signal obtained in differential laser Doppler anamometers.
the theoretical analysis of the influence of the size of scattering objects on the recorded frequency shift in laser Doppler anenometers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of the size of particles on the recorded frequency is not very significant.
the influence of the size of scattering centers on the frequency of the signal obtained in a laser Doppler system is not negligible, and it must be taken into account in the analysis of the results.
the influence of the size of scattering objects on the frequency shift in a laser Doppler system is a function of the parameters of the system and the characteristics of the scattering objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the size effect is important for the measurement of the Doppler shift in the case of small scatterers in a large scattering region and in the case of large scatterers in the case of a small scattering region.

the influence of the size of scattering objects on the frequency of a recorded signal in laser Doppler anemo­metry is a function of the ratio of the sizes of the scatterers and the spatial period of interference and the number of fringes in the scattering area.
the Doppler frequency is not a function of the size of particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the influence of the size of scattering objects on the frequency of a Doppler signal can be taken into account by introducing a correction to the Doppler shift.

the Doppler frequency is not a linear function of the scattering particle velocity, but rather a nonlinear one, and the degree of nonlinearity depends on the size and shape of the scattering particles.
in laser Doppler anemo-meters with large scattering regions the influence of the size of scattering objects on the frequency of the recorded signal is small.
